key_insight: A monolayer graphene contact layer improves light collection and electrical performance in AlInN/Si solar cells without materially changing the open-circuit voltage.
engineering_relevance: Graphene offers a low-temperature, transparent, and conductive front-contact option that can boost nitride-based solar cell efficiency.
method: Built AlxIn1-xN solar cells on p-Si(100) with a thin a-Si buffer layer
Compared three Al compositions: x = 0.22, 0.35, and 0.43
Transferred monolayer graphene onto the front surface as a semitransparent contact
evidence_signal: Photovoltaic behavior was evaluated under illumination and dark conditions, and graphene consistently increased short-circuit current density, fill factor, and power conversion efficiency across all compositions.
watch_item: The graphene transfer process and contact quality must be controlled carefully to avoid defects or nonuniform coverage that could limit reproducibility.
paper_title: Enhancement of nitride-based solar cells using graphene as transparent contact layer
